efficacy.magnitude_basis: placebo-corrected trough FEV1 versus predicted trough lung concentration / guinea-pig lung IC50, class Emax fit; the AZD3199 residual is not reported
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text and Supplementary Table S5 read. AZD3199 contributes three points (200/400/800 ug od, day 28: 99/110/97 mL at ratios 0.41/0.82/1.6) to a beta-agonist class fit; the paper reports the correlation, not a per-drug fold error, so magnitude is direction only. Member drug AZD3199 only; vilanterol, abediterol and PF-00610355 are not modelled (PF-00610355 is named once in Table S5 beside Nielsen 2012, not verified as a data row).
efficacy.reason: Reproduces known AZD3199 FEV1; no prospective call
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): the COPD trough-FEV1 data it correlates with were published (Kuna 2013, NCT00929708 results 2014-01-17) before the model, and the normalisation and Emax fits were made on them, so retro, never same. Class level: it rationalises AZD3199's flat 200-800 ug dose-response (all three doses at or above the beta-agonist half-maximal ratio) but made no prospective prediction for any member drug. Dose cell not opened: the same correlation would be counted twice; the paper's dose claim is a proposal for future drugs.
efficacy.model: AstraZeneca semi-physiological compartmental lung-PK model (rat to dog to human) normalised by guinea-pig histamine-challenge lung IC50, linking predicted human lung concentration to COPD trough FEV1 for 12 inhaled bronchodilators including AZD3199
efficacy.note: Built on published COPD data: AZD3199 200-800 ug (Kuna 2013) trough FEV1 97-110 mL at predicted lung 0.41-1.6x guinea-pig IC50 fit the beta-agonist curve.
efficacy.short: Lung-PK model refits AZD3199 trough FEV1
efficacy.quote: The model is shown to allow translation between animal species and predicts drug concentrations in human lungs that correlate with the forced expiratory volume for different classes of bronchodilators.

safety.confidence_note: Anoro Ellipta pharmacology review (study FD2008/00365/00, reviewed under IND 106,616); the quote is the first clause of a longer sentence. The study number implies 2008, but the first public record is the December 2013 review, so the track opens in 2013.
safety.judgement: Opening entry. Vilanterol's own single-agent safety pharmacology was filed under the Breo NDA, whose review is not in the bundle; the combination study reproduces the vilanterol-alone arm.
safety.model: GSK conscious telemetered beagle dog: heart rate, ECG and blood pressure after intravenous vilanterol
safety.note: Intravenous vilanterol 0.3 ug/kg drove dog heart rate from 78 to 111 bpm; 13-week dog toxicology needed a tachyphylaxis pre-dose and raised troponin I: on-target tachycardia predicted.
safety.quote: A transient increase in heart rate was observed following infusion of 0.3 µg/kg GW642444 with GSK573719 vehicle and 0.3 µg/kg GW642444 with 0.3 µg/kg GSK573719, resulting in peak increases to 111 bpm (from a mean predose of 78 bpm)

safety.magnitude_basis: heart-rate rise: +33 bpm after 0.3 ug/kg intravenous in dogs vs +17 bpm after 100 ug inhaled (4x therapeutic) in volunteers; routes and doses are not comparable
safety.confidence_note: Label section 12.2 (thorough QT study in 85 healthy volunteers; four COPD trials). The Anoro medical review reports the same for umeclidinium/vilanterol: upper 90% CI bound +10.5 bpm at 125/25 ug and +22.3 bpm at 500/100 ug.
safety.judgement: The dog predicted an on-target heart-rate rise; humans showed it at supratherapeutic doses and not at the therapeutic one, which the dog could not resolve (different route, no inhaled dose). The dog troponin rise has no patient counterpart reported, so it is not scored. Dated to December 2013 when the dog data became public.
safety.model: GSK conscious telemetered beagle dog: heart rate, ECG and blood pressure after intravenous vilanterol
safety.note: Held: heart rate rose dose-dependently in healthy volunteers (+7.8 bpm at 25 ug, +17.1 at 100 ug) and not at 25 ug in four 6-12-month COPD trials; troponin was not reported in patients.
safety.short: Dose-dependent heart-rate rise seen in humans
safety.quote: A dose-dependent increase in heart rate was also observed.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). Guinea-pig bronchoprotection t1/2 36 h, human bronchi EC50 1.9 nM with t1/2 ~690 min, and a dog safety margin of 5.6 (dose raising heart rate 5% over dose inhibiting bronchospasm 50%) are all in the abstract. No FDA filing exists; abediterol was never submitted.
safety.judgement: Opening entry; the prediction is a stated margin, so it is scored here (decision 16 counts the harm once; dose carries margin_stated).
safety.model: Almirall guinea-pig acetylcholine bronchoprotection, human isolated bronchi, and dog bronchoprotection-versus-heart-rate safety margin (abediterol)
safety.note: Dog predicted a wider heart-rate margin (5.6) than salmeterol, formoterol or indacaterol: class cardiac effects only well above bronchoprotective doses.
safety.quote: In conclusion, our results suggest that abediterol has a preclinical profile for once-daily dosing in humans together with a fast onset of action and a favorable cardiovascular safety profile.

safety.magnitude_basis: dog margin 5.6 (heart-rate dose over bronchoprotective dose) vs human systemic beta2 effects at 5-50 ug against bronchodilation from 0.625 ug; the human margin is not computable from the abstract
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). First-in-human study without a registry record found. The abstract does not give the lowest dose with palpitations, so the margin cannot be put in numbers.
safety.judgement: The model predicted class-related cardiac effects at a multiple of the effective dose, not their absence; dose-dependent mild palpitations at supra-effective doses match that in direction. Safety in healthy volunteers transfers to the COPD context.
safety.model: Almirall guinea-pig acetylcholine bronchoprotection, human isolated bronchi, and dog bronchoprotection-versus-heart-rate safety margin (abediterol)
safety.note: Held in direction: in healthy men, palpitations and tremor rose dose-dependently at 5-50 ug, above the 0.625-10 ug later effective in COPD, and were mild.
safety.short: Palpitations only at high doses, mild
safety.quote: A dose-dependent increase of systemic treatment-emergent adverse events was observed, the most frequent being palpitations, tremor, nausea, and asthenia; most were mild in intensity and resolved without the need for intervention.

safety.confidence_note: Open access (PMC4955259), abstract-level reading; single-dose exposure only (NCT01425814).
safety.reason: Dog heart-rate margin held in patients
safety.judgement: Same status; added as the first patient-level tolerability record on this track. Single-dose only, so it says nothing about chronic cardiac effects.
safety.model: Almirall guinea-pig acetylcholine bronchoprotection, human isolated bronchi, and dog bronchoprotection-versus-heart-rate safety margin (abediterol)
safety.note: In 70 COPD patients every dose 0.625-10 ug was tolerated with adverse events like placebo; the dog margin held at the doses patients used.
safety.short: All COPD doses tolerated as predicted
safety.quote: All doses of abediterol were safe and well tolerated in patients with COPD.

safety.confidence_note: Open access (PMC4027610), abstract-level reading. AZD3199 was already in a 4-week COPD trial in 2009 (NCT00929708), so the model predates its 2014 publication; 2014 is the earliest public record.
safety.judgement: Untested rather than same: the abstract gives no specific harm or margin, so the clean 4-week safety in COPD cannot be matched to a prediction. Full text (open access) was not read within budget.
safety.model: AstraZeneca guinea-pig histamine bronchoconstriction, tracheal and human bronchial ring onset, and intratracheal duration models (AZD3199)
safety.note: The model paper names 'selectivity and safety profiling' without a stated prediction; Kuna 2013 found no safety concern, but there is no model claim to compare.
safety.short: No stated safety prediction to compare
safety.quote: Determination of activities at the human β-adrenoreceptors demonstrated a series of highly potent and selective β2 receptor agonists that were progressed to further study in a guinea pig histamine-induced bronchoconstriction model.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). Guinea-pig tracheal strips are named; the in vivo duration species is not. PF-00610355 was in COPD patients from 2008 (NCT00783406), so the model predates its 2010 publication.
safety.judgement: Opening entry; the prediction is the chemistry design claim (rapid clearance keeps systemic effects low), scored here because no tolerated-dose margin was stated for dose.
safety.model: Pfizer guinea-pig tracheal-strip relaxation duration and in vivo duration-of-action models with designed rapid phase II clearance (PF-00610355)
safety.note: Pfizer designed rapid phase II clearance into PF-00610355 to minimize systemic exposure and systemic beta2 adverse events: a stated prediction of low heart-rate effects.
safety.quote: Optimization of pharmacokinetic properties was achieved through targeted introduction of a phenolic moiety to support rapid phase II clearance, thereby minimizing systemic exposure following inhalation and reducing systemically mediated adverse events.

safety.magnitude_basis: systemic beta2 harm: predicted low; observed +2.7 bpm median at 280 ug once daily, with 19% vs 8% of subjects over +20 bpm
safety.confidence_note: Open access (PMC3853534), abstract-level reading. A PK/PD meta-analysis of 13,062 heart-rate measurements from 10 studies; the underlying trials (NCT00808288, NCT00783406) posted no results.
safety.reason: Low systemic heart-rate effect as designed
safety.judgement: The design prediction (low systemic beta2 effects) held: heart-rate effects were small at up to 280 ug, several times the modelled effective fine-particle dose. The 19% vs 8% of subjects with >20 bpm rises is a partial signal, so magnitude stays direction only.
safety.model: Pfizer guinea-pig tracheal-strip relaxation duration and in vivo duration-of-action models with designed rapid phase II clearance (PF-00610355)
safety.note: Held: across 579 volunteers and patients the maximum placebo-corrected heart-rate rise in COPD was 2.7 bpm at 280 ug once daily; no relevant effect expected up to that dose.
safety.short: Heart rate +2.7 bpm at 280 ug: low
safety.quote: This PKPD analysis supports the clinical observation that no relevant effects of PF-00610355 on heart rate in COPD patients should be expected for doses up to 280 μg once daily.
